clause.text:
4.1 Party A and Party B unanimously agree that they will allocate the proceeds generated from cooperation in accordance with thefollowing provisions:

Party B shall have the right to charge, on a quarterly basis, the service fee ("Service Fee") from Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services, or designate another person to charge Service Fee from Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services. The total sum of Service Fee shall be equal to the amount of profits gained by Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services. Party B shall have the right to adjust the amount of Service Fee at its own discretion, without the prior consent of Party A or its subsidiaries.

Party A shall cause its subsidiaries to pay the Service Fee in respect of Party B's Services provided to such subsidiaries.
clause.heading: 4.1 Party A and Party B unanimously agree that they will allocate the proceeds generated from cooperation in accordance with thefollowing provisions:

reviews.rationale: The Service Fee is quarterly, lacks any payment due date or dispute-withholding right, and Party B may unilaterally adjust the amount without Party A's consent. This conflicts with the net-30/45 payment policy and the price-increase cap requiring advance notice. The uncapped unilateral adjustment leaves Party A exposed to unquantified fee increases.

citations.excerpt: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoices within thirty (30) days of receipt. Customer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith, provided it notifies Supplier of the basis for the dispute before the due date.

Fees are fixed for the Initial Term. Supplier may increase fees for a renewal term by no more than five percent (5%) over the fees for the preceding term, on at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt. Customer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith, provided it notifies Supplier of the basis for the dispute before the due date.
reviews.verification_reason: The clause supports quarterly billing, no due date or dispute right, and unilateral uncapped fee adjustment, matching the cited net-30 and price-cap policies. The quoted fallback is verbatim, and the high risk follows from the uncapped unilateral adjustment.

reviews.verification_reason: The clause addresses only payment timing and does not cap or notice fee increases, so the medium risk under the price-increase policy is correctly residual, and the verbatim fallback matches the cited playbook fallback. No unsupported claims appear.

clause.text: 4.3 Except as otherwise agreed hereunder, if Party A or its subsidiaries fail to pay the Service Fee in full on schedule according to provisions of Article 4.1 and Article 4.2, then Party A or its subsidiaries shall, in addition to the continuance of the payment of Service Fee in full, it shall pay Party B the liquidated damages at a daily interest rate of 0.03% in respect of the outstanding Service Fee.
clause.heading: 4.3 Except as otherwise agreed hereunder, if Party A or its subsidiaries fail to pay the Service Fee in full on schedule according to provisions of Article 4.1 and Article 4.2, then Party A or its subsidiaries shall, in addition to the continuance of the payment of Service Fee in full, it shall pay Party B the liquidated damages at a daily interest rate of 0.03% in respect of the outstanding Service Fee.

reviews.rationale: The clause imposes liquidated damages at 0.03% daily on late Service Fee payments, but the playbook prohibits pre-agreed sums and limits remedies to actual proven damages. The referenced Sections 4.1 and 4.2 confirm the payment obligation but contain no liquidated-damages cap or alternative remedy, leaving material exposure. Party B may also unilaterally adjust the Service Fee, and the clause lacks any cap on the daily rate.

clause.text:
5. Term of Cooperation

Party A and Party B agree and confirm that the term of cooperation under this Agreement shall commence from the execution date hereof and end on the expiration date of the operation term of Party B ("Term of Cooperation").
clause.heading: 5. Term of Cooperation

reviews.rationale: The Term of Cooperation is tied to the expiration of Party B's unspecified operation term, so the Amendment's own duration is indefinite and outside either party's control. The playbook requires a defined Initial Term and either opt-in renewal or a capped automatic renewal (renewal-opt-in), and this open-ended term conflicts with that position. Termination for convenience or cause does not cure an indefinite term, so the exposure remains material.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term and shall renew only if both parties agree in writing to renew it. Any renewal term shall not exceed twelve (12) months.

reviews.suggested_fallback: This Agreement shall renew for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term, and the fees for any renewal term shall not increase by more than five percent (5%).
reviews.verification_reason: The clause ties the Term of Cooperation to Party B's unspecified operation term, supporting the indefinite-term rationale, and the fallback quotes the [renewal-opt-in] fallback verbatim. Risk level follows reasonably, though 'high' is arguable versus playbook's medium-if-absent.

The relevant played-back policy expects termination for convenience with 30/60 days' notice; its absence creates material lock-in exposure. citations.excerpt: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party, without penalty or further liability other than for amounts accrued prior to the effective date of termination.

Either party may terminate this Agreement for cause if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure that breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party, without penalty or further liability other than for amounts accrued prior to the effective date of termination.
reviews.verification_reason: Clause 6.1 indeed restricts termination to enumerated circumstances, and the playbook marks absence of convenience and cause-cure rights as medium risk; the fallback quotes the 60-day convenience fallback verbatim. Calling it high rather than medium risk is a defensible elevation given lock-in exposure.

clause.heading: 6.1.2 One Party requests to terminate this Agreement when the other Party is declared bankrupt in accordance with the laws;

clause.heading: 6.1.3 Party B fails to provide Party B's Services to Party A for more than three consecutive years due to the force majeure event.

reviews.rationale: The clause permits termination for force majeure only after three consecutive years, far exceeding the preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day thresholds, leaving services suspended for an unreasonable period. It also omits the policy's carve-out that force majeure does not excuse payment obligations already due. This is a material deviation from force-majeure-bounded.

citations.excerpt: Neither party is liable for a failure to perform caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, provided it notifies the other party promptly and resumes performance as soon as practicable. Force majeure does not excuse an obligation to pay amounts already due, and either party may terminate if the event continues for more than sixty (60) days.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Neither party is liable for a failure to perform caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, provided it notifies the other party promptly and resumes performance as soon as practicable.
